title: Wet-felted bread basket
subtitle: A firm oval basket in natural undyed merino, fulled hard for shape retention
excerpt: Wet-felt a broad, shallow oval basket for bread or table use, about 28 cm by 20 cm and 8 cm deep. The basket is felted over a plastic bowl resist and fulled hard to produce a firm, self-supporting shape. Natural undyed merino holds its form best.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional wet-felting practice. Vessel forms over hard plastic resists are a standard wet-felting workshop project; the bread-basket shape requires a higher degree of fulling than decorative vessel forms.

glossaryTerms.definition: A felting method using hot soapy water and agitation to lock wool fibres together.
An object placed inside wet-felted roving to hold a shape during the felting process.
The vigorous stage of wet felting where the formed felt is worked hard to shrink and firm it to final dimensions.

content.text: A wet-felted bread basket is a broad, shallow vessel built over a plastic bowl
until firm enough to hold its shape with bread inside. Natural undyed

merino is the practical choice for a kitchen item: it is food-safe, durable, and shows no dye migration. The finished basket is about 28 cm by 20 cm across the opening and 8 cm deep, and shrinks to that from a much larger pre-felt piece. Allow for 30 to 40 per cent shrinkage when sizing the resist.

items.name: Plastic bowl as resist (about 34 cm by 24 cm and 11 cm deep)
Olive-oil soap dissolved in hot water
items.qty: in a large bowl or sink

items.name: Bubble wrap or bamboo mat for rolling

content.text: Place the plastic bowl upside down. Pull thin wisps of roving and lay them over the base and sides of the bowl in three full cross-hatch layers. Extend the roving about 5 cm beyond the rim of the bowl on all sides; this overhang will fold around to line the inside of the basket. Wet down the roving with warm soapy water and press gently to flatten before adding each new layer.

With the roving fully wetted, rub the surface of the bowl with a soapy hand in circular passes, working from the centre base outward to the rim. Press the felting net over the roving to keep it in position while you rub. Rub for 10 to 15 minutes until the surface is cohesive and no longer slides. Turn the bowl over carefully.
Step 3: Fold the overhang and felt the inside

Fold the roving overhang over the rim and down into the inside of the bowl. Press it flat against the interior walls. Add one more layer of roving inside the basket if the interior walls look thin. Wet down and rub the interior surface until it coheres.
Step 4: Full to a firm basket

Roll the bowl-and-felt assembly across the bamboo mat under firm pressure, alternating hot and cold rinses every few minutes. This stage takes 20 to 30 minutes of sustained rolling. The felt is adequately fulled when it springs back immediately when pressed, does not distort under the rolling pressure, and the roving layers have merged into a single dense cloth.
Step 5: Remove the resist and shape

Ease the plastic bowl out of the felt basket. The basket will hold its shape immediately if it has been fulled sufficiently. If the walls are still soft, wet and rub them by hand before the basket dries. Block the basket over the original bowl or a similar form while it dries to keep the rim level. Allow to dry fully before use, which takes 12 to 24 hours.

items.problem: The basket walls are floppy and do not hold their shape
items.cause: Insufficient fulling: the felt formed but did not shrink and stiffen to its full extent
items.fix: Return the basket to a soapy bowl of hot water, re-felt the walls vigorously by hand, then roll again. Alternating very hot and cold water shocks the fibres into further shrinkage.

items.problem: The overhang layers are detaching from the outside layers at the rim
items.cause: The overhang was not pressed firmly enough before it began to dry, or the felting on the inside was too light
items.fix: Wet the rim area thoroughly and rub the inside and outside surfaces simultaneously with your hands to lock the layers together at the rim.
